primary_sources.title: NIST DLMF 10.40, Asymptotic Expansions for Large Argument
primary_sources.use: Finite exponential Green-kernel bounds at the horizon for each fixed k; no uniform large-order numerical constant is claimed.

source_access: Primary NIST formulas opened directly; no downloaded-byte digest claimed.
strongest_comparator: The retained full coupled operator has index -1 at each admitted thermal frequency, but its kernel and precise cokernel dimension were not determined. The mixed-form and reconstruction estimates already provide uniform bounds once their frequency dependence is retained.
hardest_step: Combine those bounds into one uniform strong-operator remainder, construct a scaled compatible inverse for the minimal inverse-square operator, and control the full non-self-adjoint perturbation without choosing a self-adjoint fast phase or discarding shape feedback.
new_consequence: Above a finite uncalibrated threshold the actual auxiliary two-zero coupled operator is injective with exactly one compatibility condition and an O(gamma^-2) inverse on its range. A convergent Neumann formula fixes the normalized adjoint vector and exposes the residual of any projected solve.
scope_boundary: Only sufficiently high admitted Matsubara frequencies on the auxiliary minimal curvature/Friedrichs shape domain are covered. Neither that domain's physical admissibility nor an effective-theory frequency window is certified. No continuous causal inverse, exact nonlinear geometry or physical stability theorem is established.
regulator_contract: Keep the original state, action, clock, flux, full angular response and all residual contacts. No new finite coefficient, gravitational boundary phase, physical source projection or order reduction is adopted.
verification_scope: Exact inverse-square scaling and perturbation identities, independent Bessel Green integrals, compatible moments and Wronskians, and finite-rank perturbations of an unchanged infinite shift tail. Fixtures do not evaluate the charged Dirac kernel or certify benchmark constants.
